ghidra: read-only: no renames, comments, prototypes, function creation or saves
answer: 00B63D50 is a true affine inverse and the ledger name BSP_Matrix_BuildOrthogonalScaledAffineInverse describes its arithmetic correctly. The 145-instruction body is branch-free and leaf. It computes N[i][j] = M[j][i] / (M[j][0]^2 + M[j][1]^2 + M[j][2]^2) for i,j < 3 - the transpose of the basis with each column divided by the squared length of the source ROW it came from - then N[3][j] = -(M[3] . column j of N) for the translation, then forces the fourth column to (0,0,0,1) from the zeroed XMM0 and the float 1.0 at 00D7A24C. R*C = I exactly when the three source basis rows are mutually orthogonal and non-zero: per-axis scale and a mirrored, negative-determinant basis both invert correctly, which is what makes 'OrthogonalScaled' the right word and rules out both a plain transpose and a uniform-scale-only inverse. There is no degenerate-scale guard, no early out and no mirrored-basis path, so a sheared basis silently yields a non-inverse and a zero-length row divides by zero. It is not safe in place: 00B63E52 writes destination+10h before 00B63E5E reads source+10h.

verification.body_coverage: complete. All 145 instructions of 00B63D50..00B63F09 were read contiguously from the Ghidra listing in three pages (1-45, 45-90, 90-145) with no gap. Branch-freedom, leaf status and the absence of any EAX write were established by filtering the whole 145-instruction listing for Jcc/CALL/LOOP/EAX, not by inspecting one region.
verification.abi_evidence: SUB ESP,18h at 00B63D50 balanced by ADD ESP,18h at 00B63F06, then 00B63F09 RET with no immediate: __fastcall, no stack arguments, callee cleans nothing. First EDX use is a read (00B63D53 FLD [EDX+4]); first ECX use is a write (00B63E4B FSTP [ECX]). No EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP touched, so no saves.
verification.constants_read_from_image: 00D7A24C = 00 00 80 3f = 1.0f (float) and 00D7A250 = 00 00 00 00 00 00 f0 bf = -1.0 (double), both read with ghidra bytes rather than carried over from a prior doc.
verification.call_sites: exhaustive by construction: local/scan_b63d50_sites.py scans every E8/E9 rel32 in the PE's .text on disk for a target of 00B63D50 and returns exactly 71 sites. Ghidra's xrefs answer is capped at 25 and was not used as the set. 62 of the 71 are LEA EDX,[reg+0CCh] / LEA ECX,[reg+110h]; the nine others are tabulated in the doc.
verification.numeric: local/verify_b63d50.py re-implements the listing in Python with an explicit float32 rounding at each observed spill and multiplies M*N and N*M over 18 independently constructed yaw/pitch/roll bases x 4 scale regimes, each with a non-zero translation. Max deviation over all 16 entries: orthonormal 8.881e-07, uniform scale 2.5 8.814e-07, per-axis (0.5,3.0,1.75) 4.823e-06, mirrored (1,-1,1) 1.465e-07. Sheared rows (0.3 off-diagonal) deviate 3.000e-01 - not an inverse. Identity in gives identity out bit-exact except a -0.0f translation row from the FCHS at 00B63E9C. The FSUBP operand order (ST(1) = ST(1) - ST(0)) is confirmed by this check rather than assumed: the reversed reading would break row 3 of M*N, which comes back as (0,0,0,1).

routines.name: BSP_Matrix_BuildOrthogonalScaledAffineInverse
routines.abi: __fastcall(float* destination /*ECX*/, const float* source /*EDX*/) -> void, plain RET, EAX never written
routines.layout: row-major 4x4 float32, 16-byte row stride, row-vector convention v' = v*M. Rows 0..2 basis at +00h/+10h/+20h, translation row 3 at +30h/+34h/+38h, homogeneous column at +0Ch/+1Ch/+2Ch/+3Ch never read from the source and forced to (0,0,0,1) on the destination.
routines.layout_evidence: the +10h step between the three basis row loads (00B63D53, 00B63DA7, 00B63DF2) gives the stride; the producer at 007BEB44..007BEB6B writes the global float3 at 00F87574 into [ESI+30h/34h/38h] and then passes ESI as the source, which settles +30h..+38h as the translation row independently of this consumer.
routines.scale_handling: per-axis. Each destination column is the corresponding source row divided by that row's OWN squared length (00B63E3D..00B63E99), so three different axis scales invert correctly. A uniform scale reduces to transpose/s^2 and an orthonormal basis to the plain transpose, but the code always takes the general path.
routines.guards: none. No Jcc anywhere in the body. A zero-length row divides by zero; a sheared basis silently returns a non-inverse; a mirrored basis needs no special path and gets none.
routines.in_place: unsafe. 00B63E52 FSTP [ECX+10h] precedes 00B63E5E FLD [EDX+10h]. No call site passes the same expression for both operands.

corrections.what: docs/GUN_GRAVITY_ARC.md, the next bullet, on the mount matrix being a similarity transform
corrections.was: That mount+110h is a similarity transform, so that a unit world direction stays unit after 0042D0D0. A mount matrix with non-uniform scale would therefore distort the recovered pitch.
corrections.is: A similarity is not sufficient. A uniform scale s is a similarity and the inverse of a uniformly scaled basis scales the local direction by 1/s; 0042D0D0 is called with normalize = 0 and 00521370 takes asin of the RAW y component, so the pitch becomes asin(y/s). The required condition is an ORTHONORMAL mount basis, not merely a similarity. Yaw survives any scale that treats x and z alike, because it is an atan2.
corrections.evidence: worked through the recovered rule: a world direction at pitch 30 / yaw 36.87 returns pitch 30.000 for an identity mount, 14.478 for a uniform scale of 2, a saturated 90.000 for a uniform scale of 0.5, 14.478 for a y-only scale of 2, and yaw 14.036 instead of 36.870 for an x-only scale of 3. local/verify_b63d50.py, table in docs/MATRIX_ORTHOGONAL_INVERSE.md.

corrections.what: docs/GUN_GRAVITY_ARC.md, the 00521370 section: 'The clamp is the routine's own, applied before 0042CF10'
corrections.was: *outVert = asin( clamp(dir.y, -1.0, 1.0) ) with 00D7A250 = -1.0 and FLD1 for the upper bound, both attributed to 00521370.
corrections.is: The composed behaviour is right; the attribution is not. 00521370's FCOMI/JA at 00521380/00521382 keeps dir.y whenever dir.y > -1.0, and the FLD1 at 00521386 is compared against the constant, not against dir.y - so 00521370 applies only the lower bound and a dir.y above 1.0 passes through. The upper bound is 0042CF10's own COMISS at 0042CF19.

assumptions: Whether any mount in the shipped data actually carries a non-unit or non-orthogonal basis was NOT established. 00414DB0 composes the world matrix as local(+74h) * parent.world(+0CCh) through 00413920 and does not normalise, so nothing in the pose system enforces orthonormality. The verdict on the gravity arc's local-frame path is therefore conditional: correct for an orthonormal mount, biased by asin(y/s) otherwise.
The caller-side x87 control word. The native inherits PC/RC; the derivation assumes the MSVC default of a 64-bit mantissa and round-to-nearest.

The Python model in local/verify_b63d50.py uses Python floats where the native keeps x87 80-bit: the two additions inside each squared length and the three-term translation dot product. Products and quotients of float32 operands are provably identical under either width (64 >= 2*24+2 and 53 >= 2*24+2), so those are exact; the chained additions can differ in the last bit at extreme exponents. The C++ case has no such caveat - it calls the shipped kernel.

The producer survey is another packet's table (docs/ENTITY_LOCAL_MATRIX.md 'The producers'), re-read here but not re-derived, and the attach callers that supply localFrame at 009259C4 were not enumerated at all.

For the two register-to-register call sites and the six mixed ones, in-place use would require two different registers, or a register and a different base, to hold the same address. That this can never happen was not separately proven, so the in-place claim is 'no call site passes the same expression', not 'no call site can alias'.
0042D0D0, 00521370, 0042CF10, 00414DB0 and 00413920 were read only as far as the contract needed - partial coverage, and none of them was annotated by this packet.
BSP_Matrix_BuildOrthogonalScaledAffineInverse remains a descriptive hypothesis. This packet confirms the description is accurate; it is not a recovered symbol.

precondition_trace.question: Does the matrix the gravity arc feeds 00B63D50 satisfy the 'mutually orthogonal nonzero upper basis rows' precondition its contract requires?
precondition_trace.composition_rule_proven: 00414DB0 builds world_child = local_child * world_parent through 00413920 and never normalises. With W the parent's world basis and a_i a row of the child's local basis, (a_i W).(a_j W) = a_i (W W^T) a_j^T = sum_k a_i[k] a_j[k] w_k^2, since W W^T = diag(w_k^2) when W's own rows are orthogonal. That vanishes for orthogonal a_i, a_j only when the w_k^2 are all EQUAL. So an orthonormal chain preserves the precondition exactly; a uniformly scaled ancestor preserves it too and 00B63D50 still returns a true inverse, but the arc's pitch is then biased to asin(y/s); a per-axis scaled ancestor breaks orthogonality for every descendant whose local rotation is not axis-aligned, and then 00B63D50 is not an inverse at all and both angles are wrong. Scale anywhere in the ancestor chain suffices - it need not be on the mount itself.
precondition_trace.producer_survey: entity+74h is written wholesale by the vtable slot 88h setters 00431410 and 006E00A0 from a caller-supplied matrix. Of the four producers in docs/ENTITY_LOCAL_MATRIX.md 'The producers', NONE introduces scale of any kind: the interpolator 00904600 at 00904AE3 composes ((((RotZ*RotY)*RotX)*Translate)*record.base_20h) - pure rotations and a translation through four chained 00413920, not an element-wise lerp; the spawn/placement routine at 006E5D03 writes an identity built from 00D7A24C; unit attach 00925CE0 writes identity at 00925DCA and 00925EA0; ship motion 00825F20 never writes it. 0042D700 BSP_Matrix_ReturnIdentity4x4 and 0042D770 are identity writers on the same interface.
precondition_trace.open_link: 009259C1 LEA ECX,[ESI+74h] / 009259C4 CALL 004134F0 inside BSP_SceneNode_AttachToParents (009258F0..009259FA) copies the matrix the caller pushed at [ESP+14h] straight into +74h, unvalidated. The attach callers were NOT enumerated. So the result is 'no producer read to date puts scale into a pose local', not 'no producer can'. Follow-up packet scene_attach_local_frames.
precondition_trace.zero_length_rows: No path to the division by zero was found. +74h is the identity at construction (00925CE0 at 00925DCA and 00925EA0, docs/UNIT_INSTANCE_LAYOUT.md), so a unit's local basis is never observed all-zero, and 00955630 skips the whole local-frame path when the mount is NULL (0095576A TEST ESI,ESI, 0095578C JZ 009557F8). This is a negative search result over the unit-instance constructor, not a proof over every entity class.
precondition_trace.verdict: On the evidence available the arc's mount bases are orthonormal, so 00B63D50 returns a true inverse there and the pitch is correct in practice. That is a bounded survey resting on another packet's table plus one unread link, not a proof. The separate defect stands regardless: if a mount ever carries a uniform scale s != 1 the inverse is still correct and the pitch is still wrong, because 0042D0D0 runs with normalize = 0 and 00521370 takes asin of the raw y.

aliasing: The arc's call site does NOT alias: 0095579E LEA EDX,[ESI+0CCh] and 009557A4 LEA ECX,[ESI+110h] are 68 bytes apart on the same object and each matrix is 64 bytes, so not even partial overlap. No other caller aliases either: all 71 direct rel32 sites pass disjoint operands and none passes the same expression for both. The hazard is real in the code - 00B63E52 writes dest+10h before 00B63E5E reads src+10h - but is not exercised in the shipped binary. For the two register-to-register sites and the six mixed ones this is 'no site passes the same expression', not 'no site can alias'.
